speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To determine the cause, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or gradually, and do they fluctuate in intensity throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The symptoms of diplopia worsening with upward/downward gaze and proximal muscle weakness that fatigues after activity but improves with rest are classic for this autoimmune disorder. I am not requesting further tests as the clinical picture is sufficient for this diagnosis.
